chain.g: to strike out with the foot

ety.text: From Middle English kyken (“to strike out with the foot”), from Old Norse kikna (“to sink at the knees”) and keikja (“to bend backwards”) (compare Old Norse keikr (“bent backwards, the belly jutting forward”)), from Proto-Germanic *kaikaz (“bent backwards”), of uncertain origin. Perhaps from Proto-Germanic *kī-, *kij- (“to split, dodge, swerve sidewards”), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵeyH- (“to sprout, shoot”). Compare also Dutch kijken (“to look”), Middle Low German kīken (“to look, watch”). See keek.

senses.d: To strike or hit with the foot or other extremity of the leg.
ex: Did you kick your brother?

1895, George MacDonald, Lilith, Chapter XII: Friends and Foes,
I was cuffed by the women and kicked by the men because I would not swallow it.

senses.d: To make a sharp jerking movement of the leg, as to strike something.
ex: He enjoyed the simple pleasure of watching the kickline kick.
Sometimes we had rather rough play, for they would frequently bite and kick as well as gallop.

senses.d: To direct to a particular place by a blow with the foot or leg.
ex: Kick the ball into the goal.
Sometimes he can kick the ball forward along the ground until it is kicked in goal, where he can fall on it for a touchdown.

senses.d: To eject summarily.
ex: They are the ones who give hobbyists a bad name, and should be kicked out of any club meeting they show up at.
Dial 1-900-Mix-a-Lot and kick them nasty thoughts.

senses.d: To forcibly remove a participant from an online activity.
ex: She was kicked from the IRC server for flooding.

senses.d: To overcome (a bothersome or difficult issue or obstacle); to free oneself of (a problem).
ex: I still smoke, but they keep telling me to kick the habit.

senses.d: To move or push suddenly and violently.
ex: He was kicked sideways by the force of the blast.
The back of the car kicked out violently, forcing me to steer into the slide and accelerate in order to maintain control.

senses.d: To recoil; to push by recoiling.
ex: I asked my sister Jeanette if she wanted to shoot the 12 ga. shotgun. She replied, "does it kick"?

senses.d: To attack (a piece) in order to force it to move.
To accelerate quickly with a few pedal strokes in an effort to break away from other riders.
ex: Contador kicks again to try to rid himself of Rasmussen.

senses.d: A hit or strike with the leg, foot or knee.
ex: A kick to the knee.
A kick of his boot-heel sent the door flying into the room.

senses.d: The action of swinging a foot or leg.
ex: The ballerina did a high kick and a leap.

senses.d: A kicking motion used in a swim stroke.
ex: These boys all use a kick similar to the kick presented here however, in some cases it is less modified than in others.

senses.d: Something that tickles the fancy; something fun or amusing; a pleasure; a thrill.
ex: I finally saw the show. What a kick!
I think I sprained something on my latest exercise kick.

senses.d: The removal of a person from an online activity.
The act of restarting or resetting a watchdog timer.
Any bucking motion of an object that lacks legs or feet.
ex: The car had a nasty kick the whole way.
The pool ball took a wild kick, up off the table.

senses.d: A pungent or spicy flavour; piquancy.
ex: Add a little cascabel pepper to ordinary tomato sauce to give it a kick.
For extra kick, hollow out a lime, float it on top of the drink, and fill it with tequila.

senses.d: A stimulation provided by an intoxicating substance.
A pass played by kicking with the foot.
To die.
To be emphatically excellent.
ex: That band really kicks.

senses.d: Terrific, great (of clothes) smart, fashionable.
ex: a kicking pair of jeans
a kicking party

senses.d: Alive, active (especially in the phrase alive and kicking).
ex: still kicking at 89 years old

senses.d: Actively ongoing and enjoyable.
The action of the verb to kick.
ex: In boxing, kicking one's opponent is not allowed.

senses.d: A violent assault involving repeated kicks.
ex: The bullies pushed the boy over and gave him a kicking.

senses.d: A great loss or defeat; licking.
A performance art that is a mix of dance footwork, acrobatic maneuver, and martial arts kicks, drawn from a variety of disciplines. Used in stage dance choreography and staged fight choreography.
